findings.title: ESP tunnel using 64-bit block cipher
findings.subject: 203.0.113.7->198.51.100.4:0xe88b7591
findings.detail: Packet framing on this SA matches block 8, IV 8, ICV 12, which identifies 3DES-CBC / HMAC-MD5-96 or DES-CBC / HMAC-SHA1-96 (framing-identical, not separable passively). 64-bit block size is vulnerable to Sweet32 birthday collisions on long-lived tunnels; both DES and 3DES are withdrawn. Inferred from 380 packets at 100% confidence in the framing class.
findings.reference: RFC 4303 s2; RFC 8221; NIST SP 800-77 Rev. 1 s4.1
findings.remediation: Reconfigure the child SA proposal to AES-GCM-256 and confirm from the gateway's own SA table.

Traffic crosses the link in plaintext and is readable by anyone on path. Inferred from 380 packets at 100% confidence in the framing class.
findings.reference: RFC 4303 s2; RFC 8221; NIST SP 800-77 Rev. 1 s4.1

findings.title: IKEv1 Aggressive Mode
findings.detail: Aggressive Mode transmits the responder's identity and a hash derived from the pre-shared key in the clear, in the first two messages. Anyone who can capture the handshake can mount an offline dictionary attack against the PSK without touching the gateway.
findings.reference: NIST SP 800-77 Rev. 1 s3.2.1; RFC 2409 s5.4
findings.remediation: Disable Aggressive Mode. Use IKEv2 with certificate authentication, or at minimum IKEv1 Main Mode with a high-entropy PSK.

findings.title: Prohibited IKE encryption algorithm: 3DES_CBC
findings.detail: 64-bit block invites Sweet32 birthday collisions; MUST NOT per RFC 8247. This protects the IKE control channel itself, so a break exposes the negotiated child SA keys.
findings.remediation: Configure AES-GCM-256, or AES-CBC-256 where AEAD is unavailable.

findings.title: Prohibited IKE encryption algorithm: ENCR_3DES
findings.detail: 64-bit block invites Sweet32 birthday collisions; MUST NOT per RFC 8247. This protects the IKE control channel itself, so a break exposes the negotiated child SA keys.
findings.remediation: Configure AES-GCM-256, or AES-CBC-256 where AEAD is unavailable.

findings.title: Prohibited Diffie-Hellman group 2 (1024-bit MODP)
findings.detail: 1024-bit MODP: within reach of nation-state precomputation (Logjam). A single precomputation against a standard modulus breaks every session that ever used it, including traffic already recorded.
findings.reference: RFC 8247 s2.4; NIST SP 800-77 Rev. 1 s3.3
findings.remediation: Configure Group 19 (256-bit ECP) or Group 14 at minimum.

findings.title: Prohibited Diffie-Hellman group 2 (1024-bit MODP)

findings.reference: RFC 8247 s2.4; NIST SP 800-77 Rev. 1 s3.3
findings.remediation: Configure Group 19 (256-bit ECP) or Group 14 at minimum.

findings.title: Association provides only 64-bit security
findings.detail: Component strengths: encryption 112 bits, prf 64 bits, integrity 64 bits, key_exchange 80 bits. The association is bounded by its prf at 64 bits, which is graded 'broken'. A strong cipher does not compensate for a weak key exchange: an attacker who recovers the session key never has to attack the cipher at all.
findings.remediation: Raise the prf to at least the 128-bit level. The whole suite should be re-specified together rather than patched component by component.

A strong cipher does not compensate for a weak key exchange: an attacker who recovers the session key never has to attack the cipher at all.
findings.remediation: Raise the prf to at least the 128-bit level. The whole suite should be re-specified together rather than patched component by component.

findings.title: 64-bit block cipher already exceeds the Sweet32 birthday bound
findings.detail: The negotiated cipher has a 64-bit block, so ciphertext blocks begin colliding after roughly 34.4 GB under a single key. With a 48-hour rekey interval this SA processes about 1091.79 GB per key, which is 31.775x the bound. At the observed 50.55 Mbps this SA reaches the bound 91 minutes after each rekey.
findings.remediation: Move to a 128-bit block cipher (AES-GCM-256). If that cannot be scheduled immediately, cut the rekey interval so that less than 34.4 GB passes under any single key — that is mitigation, not a fix.

findings.title: 64-bit block cipher already exceeds the Sweet32 birthday bound
findings.detail: The negotiated cipher has a 64-bit block, so ciphertext blocks begin colliding after roughly 34.4 GB under a single key. With a 24-hour rekey interval this SA processes about 455.96 GB per key, which is 13.27x the bound. At the observed 42.22 Mbps this SA reaches the bound 109 minutes after each rekey.
findings.remediation: Move to a 128-bit block cipher (AES-GCM-256). If that cannot be scheduled immediately, cut the rekey interval so that less than 34.4 GB passes under any single key — that is mitigation, not a fix.

findings.title: ESP payload entropy below the ciphertext floor
findings.subject: 203.0.113.90->198.51.100.12:0xc553ab9a
findings.detail: Mean payload entropy is 5.44 bits/byte. Output of any sound cipher is statistically indistinguishable from random and sits above 7.9. This SA is carrying structured data, which points to ESP-NULL, a compression layer, or a misconfigured transform.
findings.remediation: Verify the SA's encryption transform on the gateway; ESP-NULL must not be used on transit links.

findings.title: IKEv1 in use
findings.detail: The gateway negotiated IKEv1, which has been formally deprecated. It has no built-in DoS cookie mechanism, no reliable fragmentation, and no path to the RFC 8784 post-quantum pre-shared key extension.
findings.reference: RFC 9395 (IKEv1 deprecation); NIST SP 800-77 Rev. 1 s3.2
findings.remediation: Migrate the tunnel to IKEv2 and disable IKEv1 on the gateway.

findings.title: Prohibited integrity algorithm: AUTH_HMAC_MD5
findings.detail: MD5 is collision-broken; MUST NOT per RFC 8247
findings.remediation: Configure AUTH_HMAC_SHA2_256_128 or stronger.

findings.title: Prohibited PRF: PRF_HMAC_MD5
findings.detail: MD5-based PRF, MUST NOT per RFC 8247
findings.remediation: Configure PRF_HMAC_SHA2_256 or stronger.

findings.title: Prohibited integrity algorithm: AUTH_HMAC_MD5_96
findings.detail: MD5 is collision-broken; MUST NOT per RFC 8247
findings.remediation: Configure AUTH_HMAC_SHA2_256_128 or stronger.

findings.title: Prohibited PRF: PRF_HMAC_MD5
findings.detail: MD5-based PRF, MUST NOT per RFC 8247
findings.remediation: Configure PRF_HMAC_SHA2_256 or stronger.

findings.title: Association provides only 96-bit security
findings.detail: Component strengths: encryption 128 bits, prf 96 bits, integrity 96 bits, key_exchange 112 bits. The association is bounded by its prf at 96 bits, which is graded 'deprecated'. A strong cipher does not compensate for a weak key exchange: an attacker who recovers the session key never has to attack the cipher at all.
findings.remediation: Raise the prf to at least the 128-bit level. The whole suite should be re-specified together rather than patched component by component.

findings.title: ESP tunnel using AES-CBC with 96-bit ICV
findings.subject: 203.0.113.21->198.51.100.33:0xd36897e4
findings.detail: Packet framing on this SA matches block 16, IV 16, ICV 12, which identifies AES-CBC-128 / HMAC-SHA1-96. SHA-1 truncated to 96 bits; CBC lacks integrated authentication. Inferred from 380 packets at 100% confidence in the framing class.
findings.reference: RFC 4303 s2; RFC 8221; NIST SP 800-77 Rev. 1 s4.1
findings.remediation: Reconfigure the child SA proposal to AES-GCM-256 and confirm from the gateway's own SA table.

findings.title: Pre-shared key authentication (PRE_SHARED_KEY)
findings.detail: PSK authentication is offline-crackable if a handshake is captured. On a backbone link this is a credential-management liability: the same secret is typically shared across peers and rarely rotated.
findings.remediation: Move to certificate-based authentication (RSA or ECDSA) backed by the agency PKI.

findings.title: Deprecated integrity algorithm: AUTH_HMAC_SHA1_96
findings.detail: SHA-1 is deprecated for new systems (SP 800-131A Rev. 2)
findings.remediation: Migrate to AUTH_HMAC_SHA2_256_128.

findings.title: No quantum-resistant key establishment
findings.detail: The SA relies entirely on classical Diffie-Hellman. Traffic recorded today can be decrypted once a cryptanalytically relevant quantum computer exists, which matters for material whose sensitivity outlives the hardware.
findings.remediation: Deploy an RFC 8784 post-quantum pre-shared key now, and enable a hybrid ML-KEM key exchange (Group 35-37) as gateway firmware allows.

findings.title: Broken transforms remain in the proposal set
findings.detail: The initiator advertised transforms that policy prohibits: AUTH_HMAC_MD5_96, DH group 2, ENCR_3DES. Even unselected, they widen the downgrade surface — an on-path attacker who can drop the strong proposals may force a fallback.
findings.remediation: Prune the gateway's transform set to approved algorithms only, so a downgrade has nothing to fall back to.

findings.title: Excessive SA lifetime (48.0 hours)
findings.detail: The SA is configured to live 48.0 hours before rekey. Long lifetimes increase the volume of traffic under a single key and lengthen the window in which a compromised key stays useful.
findings.remediation: Reduce the IKE SA lifetime to 24 hours or less, and the child SA to 8 hours.

findings.title: Repeated negotiation failures observed
findings.detail: The exchange carried NO_PROPOSAL_CHOSEN. In isolation this is a misconfiguration; in volume it is the signature of an attacker probing which proposals a gateway will accept, or brute-forcing authentication.
findings.remediation: Correlate against the gateway's own logs and rate-limit IKE from untrusted sources. If unexplained, treat as reconnaissance.

findings.title: Deprecated PRF: PRF_HMAC_SHA1
findings.detail: SHA-1-based PRF is deprecated for new systems
findings.remediation: Configure PRF_HMAC_SHA2_256.

findings.title: IKEv2 fragmentation not negotiated
findings.detail: Neither peer advertised RFC 7383 fragmentation. Certificate-bearing IKE_AUTH messages then rely on IP fragmentation, which middleboxes on carrier paths routinely drop — a common cause of tunnels that establish with PSK but fail with certificates.
findings.remediation: Enable IKEv2 fragmentation on both peers before migrating to certificate auth.

phases.action: Replace broken classical cryptography first. These links are exposed to a conventional attacker today, so the quantum timeline is not the binding constraint — fix them regardless of PQC readiness.
